# 03 Lay out a core sequence diagram: lanes, lifelines, message positions

## Outcome

A new `layoutSequence(model, options)` computes participant lane x-positions (first-declaration
order, sized from measured label width), full-height lifeline y-extents, and each message's
y-coordinate, arrow endpoint x-coordinates (source/target lane centers, offset for self-messages),
and label position — for the core subset (no blocks/create/box geometry yet — tickets 08/13 extend
this same module).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `layoutSequence` on a hand-built core `SequenceModel` (participants + messages + optional
  title) returns a `PositionedSequenceDiagram` with one `PositionedParticipant` per participant,
  each with a distinct, non-overlapping `x` in declaration order, and a `width`/`height` sized to
  its label plus padding.
- [ ] Each `PositionedMessage` has a y-coordinate strictly greater than every message declared
  before it (top-to-bottom document order), and endpoint x-coordinates matching its `from`/`to`
  participants' lane centers.
- [ ] A self-message (`from === to`) produces a distinct point path that loops out and back to the
  same lane rather than a zero-length path.
- [ ] The returned `width`/`height` bounds every participant and message computed.
- [ ] `title`, when present, contributes to `height` (reserves space above the first participant
  row) and is carried through to `PositionedSequenceDiagram.title` unchanged.
- [ ] Uses the same `TextMeasurer` seam as `layoutGraph` (a fake deterministic measurer in tests,
  matching `layoutGraph.test.ts`'s existing fixture pattern).

## Test seam

`layoutSequence(model: SequenceModel, options: { measureText: TextMeasurer }):
PositionedSequenceDiagram` — unit level, pure function, fake deterministic `TextMeasurer`.
